title: Finite free coefficient and localized morphism descent of reindexed evaluation
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_W$, $R_W=\lim_n B_{W,n}$ for a scheme $W$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $g:X\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ be a scheme isomorphism, with $\ell$ invertible on both schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $F=g^{-1}$, with the coefficient identifications induced by all quotient projections. Use the coefficient-stage derived operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

For a finite coefficient extension $E\subset L$, put $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}$ and use the finite-free completed scalar comparison [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] and the operation scalar comparisons [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. For arbitrary ambient $R_Y$-complexes $M,N$, the evaluation-normalized comparison
$$H_{R_Y}(M,N)\otimes^L_{R_Y}S_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{S_Y}(S_Y\otimes^L_{R_Y}M,S_Y\otimes^L_{R_Y}N)$$
is an isomorphism; on derived-complete constructible inputs the ordinary extensions are identified with the specified completed ones. Under the derived scalar adjunction of [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction], its restriction is the finite-biproduct comparison $H_{R_Y}(M,N)\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y\cong H_{R_Y}(M,N\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y)$. On a finite free basis it is a direct sum of copies of the ambient Hom comparison, and evaluation has formula $(f\otimes s)(x\otimes t)=f(x)\otimes st$. The map is independent of the basis by its evaluation-transpose normalization, commutes with reindexing $F$ (which fixes coefficient scalars), and respects $E\subset L\subset L'$ by associativity of scalar multiplication and tensor reassociation, with identity for $L=E$. No perfectness is imposed, and this includes ramified finite extensions.

Write $c^0_{g;M,N}:FH_{R_Y}(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{R_X}(FM,FN)$ for the ambient reindexing comparison of [lem-pod-reindexing-hom-resolution-model], with its restriction and completed evaluation/transposition identities on constructible-Hom pairs as specified in [lem-pod-reindexing-completed-evaluation-reflection]. This integral comparison and these identities extend to the rational categories of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] on their stated constructible-Hom domains. Naturality and evaluation hold for arbitrary localized arrows $a=\sum_i a_i\otimes\lambda_i$, $b=\sum_j b_j\otimes\nu_j$, with each integral equation extended by the factors $\lambda_i\nu_j$; transposition is linear in its input. Inverses, signed shifts and scheme-composition equations localize too. Under the finite scalar comparisons just specified these maps and equations agree at every larger finite field. Thus in the common-stage categories of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] they define natural maps independent of representatives: every finite diagram of objects and arrows is represented at a common finite field, and representatives equal at a further field have equal images there. Their classes preserve evaluation, transposition, inverses, both Hom shifts and scheme composition, with exactly the localized and common-stage operation normalizations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

The map scalarHomOrdinary is, by definition, the closed transpose of scalar-extended evaluation, so applying the inverse transpose gives its displayed normalization. proof.text:
Put $H=H_{R_Y}(M,N)$. For a basis of the finite-free $R_Y$-module $S_Y$, use the specified basis isomorphisms $a_H:H^d\xrightarrow{\sim}U_YT_YH$ and $a_N:N^d\xrightarrow{\sim}U_YT_YN$. Let $\beta:U_YH_{S_Y}(T_YM,T_YN)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{R_Y}(M,U_YT_YN)$ be the evaluation-normalized scalar adjunction. The coordinates lemma gives, for each inclusion $\iota_i$,
$$\beta\,U_Y(\gamma)\,a_H\,\iota_i=H_{R_Y}(M,a_N\iota_i).$$
Thus the finite coproduct universal property identifies $\beta U_Y(\gamma)$, after $a_H,a_N$, with the finite-biproduct comparison. Both basis maps have the lemma's scalar-section normalization; neither is chosen using invertibility of $\gamma$. Finite freeness makes tensor with $S_Y$ this exact finite direct sum, so the ordinary tensor notation computes its derived functor here.

proof.text: Use the normalized representative evaluation $f\otimes x\mapsto f(x)$ and the scalar tensor comparison $1\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(1\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. The transpose defining $\gamma$ therefore sends $(f\otimes s,x\otimes t)$ to $f(x)\otimes st$. More precisely this is the formula on sheafified pure-tensor summands of the total complexes, followed by the prescribed localized augmentation; it does not assert that every derived arrow is a literal section $f$. There is no new sign from $s,t$, which have degree zero; reversing the evaluation factors uses the same Koszul symmetry on both sides. The definition as evaluation transpose makes $\gamma$ independent of the temporary basis.

source.place: Step 5, coefficient transport; explicit agent refinement

proof.text:
Write $F_R,F_S$ for reindexing at the two coefficient rings and $b_Z:T_XF_RZ\xrightarrow{\sim}F_ST_YZ$ for the normalized scalar/reindexing tensor map. Its K-flat chain model and quotient compatibility are supplied by the isomorphism-scalar-tensor lemma. Set $H=H_{R_Y}(M,N)$. The two scalar/reindexing routes into $H_{S_X}(F_ST_YM,F_ST_YN)$ are
$$p=c^S F_S(\gamma_Y)b_H,\qquad q=H_{S_X}(b_M^{-1},b_N)\gamma_X T_X(c^R).$$
Compare their transposes under the $S_X$ tensor-Hom adjunction, on the same domain $F_ST_YM\otimes_{S_X}^LT_XF_RH$. Expand $\gamma$ by its evaluation-transpose definition and $c$ by its reindexing evaluation equation. Both transposes are $F_ST_Y(\operatorname{ev})$ preceded by the same balanced scalar/tensor and reindexing associations: on common K-flat tensor and Hom representatives both send $(F(m)\otimes t,F(f)\otimes s)$ to $F(f(m))\otimes st$. This is equality of the sheafified maps on every homogeneous total-tensor summand before localization; the signed symmetry is identical on both paths, and scalar factors have degree zero. The cited representative models include the same localized target augmentation, so the transposes agree in $D(S_X)$. The adjunction bijection gives $p=q$ there. This also proves evaluation compatibility, and applying the same bijection to a map and its transpose proves transposition compatibility. Restriction of scalars is not used to detect equality.

proof.text: The completion-unit normalization used below is explicit. Put $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_L$. The DVR theorem gives $t=uv^e$ with $u$ a unit and $e\geq1$ (its absolute value in $L$ is less than $1$). The principal Koszul replacement lemma gives injectivity of $t,v$ on the corresponding completed rings and identifies their quotients with the prescribed constant quotient sheaves. Countable products are exact for each of these module categories and for abelian sheaves (apply the same product theorem to the constant ring $\mathbf Z$). Together with finite freeness from Step 1 these verify every hypothesis of completion exchange. Its actual map $\epsilon:T_WC_R\cong C_ST_W$ satisfies $\epsilon\,T_W\eta^R=\eta^S T_W$. The ambient-operation model identifies $C_R(M\otimes^L N)$ with the specified completed tensor, preserving the quotient augmentation. These give the unit-preserving exchange needed in the next step; they do not by themselves identify a chosen scalar-operation comparison.

source.place: Step 5, coefficient transport; explicit agent refinement

proof.text:
Write $C_W$ for specified integral scalar extension, $\chi:T_W\xrightarrow{\sim}C_W$ on complete inputs, and $\eta^R_{M,N}:M\otimes^LN\to M\widehat\otimes^LN$ for the ordinary-to-completed tensor unit. Apply the normalized-scalar-realization lemma with $f=1_W$ to pin $\theta^\otimes$: its statement identifies this specified comparison with realization of the balanced tensor map $\sigma^D$ on entire quotient systems. Under the ambient-operation models and completion exchange of Step 6 this is the same map induced by the normalized scalar tensor comparison; after composing with the specified arithmetic-subsequence Roos quasi-isomorphisms of the exchange, both apply quotient tensor association to both product coordinates; invert these quasi-isomorphisms afterwards. This does not identify equal powers of the two uniformizers. On simultaneous K-flat quotient presentations these associations send $(m\otimes n)\otimes s$ to $(m\otimes1)\otimes(n\otimes\bar s)$; on the quotient augmentation the shifted-product coordinate is zero. Thus the following is an equality of these specified derived maps:
$$\theta^\otimes_{M,N}\chi_{M\widehat\otimes N}T_W(\eta^R_{M,N})=\eta^S_{C_WM,C_WN}(\chi_M\otimes\chi_N)\mu_{M,N}.$$
Here $\mu:T_W(M\otimes^LN)\cong T_WM\otimes^LT_WN$. This uses the lemma's entire-system localization and realization, not a claim that evaluations at finite levels detect derived-system morphisms.

proof.text:
Identify the pullback comparison of the reindexing-completion lemma with the specified $\kappa$ of inverse-image-pullback-comparison(b). On the same K-flat resolution $P\to K$, both are represented by
$$z\longmapsto(0,(F(z\bmod\varpi^n)\otimes1)_n)$$
into the same quotient-pullback Roos cone, followed by the inverse localized $F(P)\to F(K)$. This is equality of chain maps with both coordinates fixed, so their localized morphisms coincide. The specified-pullback-alpha lemma pins $\theta^{g^*}=\alpha$ to its actual cone map $\delta_P$ and completion maps. The isomorphism-comparison-scalar lemma then gives
$$\alpha_K C_X(\kappa^E_K)=\kappa^L_{C_YK}\beta_K,\qquad \beta_K=F_S(\chi_{Y,K})b_K\chi_{X,F_RK}^{-1}.$$
Its hypotheses hold for the constructible complete objects under consideration, including their constructible Hom outputs. Thus $F\cong Lg^*$ in this item has exactly this scalar comparison. Under that identification the tensor comparison is the specified one by the reindexing-completion lemma. No arbitrary identification of the two pullback functors is substituted.

source.place: Step 5, coefficient transport; repair of returned scalar-comparison normalization

proof.text:
Restrict now to $M,N$ with constructible integral Hom. Apply the new specified-Hom-scalar-evaluation lemma on $W=X,Y$; these are arbitrary schemes with $\ell$ invertible, with no finite-type or finite-field-base hypothesis needed. It gives
$$\theta^{\mathcal Hom}\chi_H=H_S(\chi_M^{-1},\chi_N)\gamma.$$
The completed-evaluation-reflection lemma supplies the integral $c^0$, inverse, naturality, signed shifts and scheme composition, and the bijection obtained by precomposing with the ordinary-to-completed tensor unit. Therefore the scalar evaluation square follows from the ordinary one in Step 4: use the pinned Hom formula above and the tensor-unit equation in Step 7, precompose both routes with that unit, and cancel via the reflector bijection (the target is complete). Transposition follows from its second adjunction bijection. In the pullback coordinates of Step 8 the comparison is $H(\kappa_M^{-1},\kappa_N)c^0\kappa_H^{-1}$. Substituting the equation $\alpha C\kappa=\kappa\beta$ and the displayed Hom pin into Step 4 proves its scalar square with precisely $\theta^{g^*}$ and $\theta^{\mathcal Hom}$. Naturality of $\chi$ cancels the intervening units. Hence all scalar squares use the specified three operation comparisons, rather than families known only to exist with tower laws. The integral-operation scalar lemma states that C preserves constructibility; the Hom pin identifies H_S(CM,CN) with C H_R(M,N), so the scalar-extended pairs remain in this domain. For integral_pair_permitted, choose the coherent family and comparison from [lem-pod-reindexing-completed-evaluation-reflection]. Its ordinary-to-completed components are invertible on each constructible input. The same node proves constructibility of ordinary reindexed Hom. Apply internal Hom to the inverse first component and direct second component to transport this constructibility to the specified completed pullback inputs. For integral_comparison_existsUnique with arbitrary law-bearing A and T, sfDerivedComplete_iff_legacy converts constructible completeness into the completeness predicate in A.CompleteUnit. The defining completion-unit composite is therefore invertible. Conjugate the ambient homComparison by inverse kappa on the Hom output, inverse kappa on the first input, and direct kappa on the second input. Fullness restricts this isomorphism. Naturality of kappa, its inverse square, and reindexing_laws naturality prove naturality of the restricted comparison. Cancellation of the invertible output kappa and the first-input Hom image proves the required normalization and uniqueness. This obligation does not need the scalar-completion exchange construction in Steps 6--8.

proof.text: Rationalization has the same objects and Hom modules $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal I}(A,B)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$. Define $c_E=c^0\otimes1$ and its inverse by the integral inverse tensored with $1$. The prescribed operation formulas are $F(a\otimes\lambda)=F(a)\otimes\lambda$ and $H(a\otimes\lambda,b\otimes\nu)=H(a,b)\otimes\lambda\nu$, extended additively. They are balanced because the integral actions are linear in each variable, including the contravariant first Hom variable: moving $r\in\mathcal O_E$ from an integral arrow to its coefficient multiplies the output by the same $r$. Thus these formulas act on the tensor products themselves, independently of an expression as a sum. No injectivity of the integral-to-rational Hom map is used. Rationalize kappa as well: when the pullback operation is written as Lg^*, use the transported comparison displayed in Step 9.

proof.text: For $a=\sum_i a_i\otimes\lambda_i:M'\to M$ and $b=\sum_j b_j\otimes\nu_j:N\to N'$, expand the two sides of the naturality equation for $c_E$. The $(i,j)$ terms are the integral naturality equation multiplied by $\lambda_i\nu_j$, so they agree. Expand the completed evaluation square in exactly the same way, using the integral evaluation square of Step 9; each term again has this product coefficient. The tensor-Hom transpose is linear in its single input, so for $z=\sum_k z_k\otimes\rho_k$ define $z^\sharp=\sum_k z_k^\sharp\otimes\rho_k$. Integral transposition is linear (it is the Hom-complex adjunction), and the inverse adjunction is linear too; hence these are well-defined inverse maps and its transport equation follows term by term. These computations cover all localized arrows, not just images of integral ones. Once rationalComparison is packaged as the natural isomorphism of Step 10, its rational_naturality equation is obtained directly by applying its hom.naturality to the full-subcategory arrow (a.op,b). This includes arbitrary localized arrows without choosing tensor presentations again.

proof.text: Composition in the localized category is bilinear. Thus the two inverse equations become $(c^0)^{-1}c^0\otimes1=1$ and $c^0(c^0)^{-1}\otimes1=1$. For either signed Hom shift and for scheme composition, the integral equations of Step 9 are equations between composites of integral components; replacing each component by its tensor with $1$ gives the same equations. Naturality against arbitrary shifted arrows follows by the expansion of Step 11, since the prescribed shift is linear. The scalar squares of Steps 4–9 rationalize in the same manner, using the scalar-extension formula $(f\otimes a)\mapsto T_{L/E}(f)\otimes a$ with $a\in E\subset L$. Consequently all the rational maps and equations agree after every finite coefficient extension, with their specified identity and tower comparisons. The tower and identity equations are those of the specified operation comparisons in the integral-operation scalar lemma; the pins in Steps 7–9 identify our scalar squares with those maps. For the integral signed-shift interface, the signed ambient Hom isomorphism of [lem-pod-reindexing-evaluation-shift-composition] and shift-stability from [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated] prove that the shifted pair is permitted. Fullness restricts that same isomorphism; equality of underlying homs proves uniqueness. Rational permitted pairs follow from integral_pair_permitted by the literal object equation of rationalDerivedPullback.

proof.text: For common-stage inputs with fields $E_1,E_2$, put $K=E_1E_2$. Construct the comparison at $K$ using the rational map just obtained. At a larger field $L$, conjugate $c_L$ by the scalar comparisons of its source and target operations, exactly as prescribed for operation arrows. Step 12 says this conjugate equals scalar extension of $c_K$. The identity and tower equations make the same assertion for any further $L'$. A finite collection of objects and arrow representatives has finitely many fields, whose compositum is a common field by the coefficient-category definition. If two representatives are equal at a further field, their operation images are equal there, and the conjugated comparisons are equal there by the scalar square. Hence their colimit classes are equal. This proves independence of fields and representatives without requiring transition functors to be faithful. For common_pair_permitted specifically, work with the integral objects underlying the rational pair at the input compositum. The stage-system transition formula identifies these with the specified integral scalar extensions. The object formula for rational pullback and integralPullbackScalarComparison identify the pulled-back objects at that same compositum with the integral pullbacks of the original stage objects. Apply integral_pair_permitted there, and transport constructibility through internal Hom, using the first-variable isomorphism oppositely and the inverse second-variable isomorphism. The proved object-normalization interface [lem-pod-common-stage-operation-object-normalizations] records the three literal object formulas without unfolding the chosen functors in the equality-only copyObj transports.

proof.text: Represent each naturality, evaluation, transposition, inverse, signed-shift or scheme-composition diagram at one common finite field (enlarging it for the finitely many arrows in that diagram). There it is one of the rational equations of Steps 11–12. Apply the Hom-colimit structure maps to that equality. Intermediate scalar comparisons cancel with their inverses, and the tower equation identifies successive changes with the direct one, so the resulting equality is precisely the equation between the normalized common-stage operations, including the specified evaluation and transpose. This proves all asserted common-stage laws. The same argument applies only on the specified constructible-Hom pairs; no closure of arbitrary constructible pairs under Hom is asserted. The common_tensorComparison interface is obtained directly from canonicalCommonStagePullbackTensor in [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], transporting only its source and target object equalities. Substitution of these equalities reduces existence and uniqueness to the original isomorphism and Iso.ext. The common_signedShift_images equation is the image of rational_signed_shifts under the stage inclusion, by Functor.congr_map followed by rational_signed_shifts, whose displayed parameters are inferred from the goal and whose normalization hypotheses are already in context. The common_transposition equation can then be proved without another representative calculation: copied pullback and tensor functors equal their original functors by Functor.ext_of_iso. Transport the natural tensor isomorphism of lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso across these equalities. Its prescribed component HEq identifies the resulting naturality equation with commonTensorComparison. Use common_transpose_existsUnique to characterize the desired transpose by evaluation; expand tensor functoriality, precompose with the invertible tensor comparison, apply its naturality and common_evaluation, and cancel the tensor comparison. The defining evaluation equation of the original transpose closes the remaining equality.
